messages.text: Somerset pair Overton and Luff win PCA awards

metadata.summary: Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff have won the headline accolades at the 2026 PCA awards in partnership with Toyota while emerging England stars Sonny Baker and Tilly Corteen-Coleman also received coveted honours at Exhibition White City.
metadata.content: 2026 PCA awards: Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff win headline accolades at Exhibition White City | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content 2026 PCA awards: Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff win headline accolades at Exhibition White City Craig Overton and Sophie Luff win the headline accolades at the 2026 PCA awards to complete a Somerset double; England's Sonny Baker and left-arm spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman claim Young Player of the Year awards Wednesday 30 September 2026 16:57, UK Image: Craig Overton and Sophie Luff won the headline accolades at Exhibition White City on Wednesday Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff have won the headline accolades at the 2026 PCA awards in partnership with Toyota while emerging England stars Sonny Baker and Tilly Corteen-Coleman also received coveted honours at Exhibition White City. Overton saw him collect a PCA awards quadruple, winning the PCA Men's Player of the Year trophy, the PCA Men's Domestic Overall MVP, the Rothesay County Championship Player of the Year and selection in the IG PCA Men's Team of the Year. The 32-year-old, who has scored 951 runs, taken 76 wickets and 45 catches across all three formats this season, becomes the first Somerset player to secure the award since Nick Compton in 2012, beating competition from the notable shortlist of players including Joe Clarke, George Hill and Dan Lawrence. Reports of a rift between Ronaldo and Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus emerged after the six-time Ballon d'Or winner was left as an unused substitute in Sunday's Nations League win over Norway. Jesus, who was Ronaldo's coach at Al Nassr, insisted "there was no incident whatsoever" in his press conference on Wednesday, claiming the star was set to return to training with his team-mates ahead of Thursday's Nations League game against Denmark in Copenhagen. messages.text: What if Man City's Premier League titles and trophies are stripped?

metadata.summary: Jamie Carragher has called for Manchester City to be stripped of their titles after the club was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules – so what would change?
metadata.content: Man City charges: What if club's Premier League titles and trophies are stripped? Who 'benefits' and what changes? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Man City charges: What if club's Premier League titles and trophies are stripped? Who 'benefits' and what changes? Manchester City won three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, three League Cups and one Community Shield between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons during which they committed serious breaches of Premier League financial rules; Man City deny the breaches and will appeal against the ruling Wednesday 30 September 2026 19:52, UK Image: Vincent Kompany lifts the Premier League trophy after winning the title with Man City in 2014 Jamie Carragher has called for Manchester City to be stripped of their titles after the club was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules – so what would change? An independent commission found City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, during which the club won three Premier League titles, one FA Cup, three League Cups and one Community Shield. Sanctions will be addressed in a further hearing with the independent commission and Man City, who continue to deny the breaches, have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday, October 2 to do so.
